nodes.title: Stage 2 Input Guide · Panel Count / 3-Panel Layout / Props
widgets_values:
# Stage 2 input · how many panels, and how to arrange them

1. **Panel Count** — pick 1 to 4.
2. **3-Panel Layout** — only used when you picked 3.
   - `OFF` : one tall panel on the left + two stacked on the right
   - `ON` : one wide panel on top + two side by side below
3. **Pose photo** — used to set the action in Panel 1.
4. **Prop Mode `OFF`** — Panel 2 just displays the prop on its own.
5. **Prop Mode `ON`** — the character actually uses the prop in Panels 1 and 2.
6. Anything else you want goes into **⑧**.

When a prop switch is OFF, its prompt text is removed automatically.

subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the adult character shown in <Picture 1>. <Picture 1> is the Stage 1 turnaround sheet that shows this same character from the front, the side and the back (plus a chest-up close-up when the 4-panel layout was used). Its reference role is the COMPLETE CHARACTER: face, facial geometry, hair, costume as seen from every angle, colors, materials, body proportions and rendering style. Use all three views to understand the character; never reproduce the three-view sheet layout itself and never paste any of its views.

summary:
[reference generation] One static high-resolution character contact sheet of <Subject 1>, divided into exactly the number of panels given by SELECTED PANEL COUNT below.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in every character panel): fully_preserved - remains the same character from <Picture 1> in every panel, preserving the exact face, hair, costume, colors, materials and body proportions. Each additional attached picture is bound to exactly one role line below by its <Picture N> tag and contributes only its own named prop, accessory or environment and never replaces or restyles <Subject 1>.

detailed_description:
The target is one still image, not a video. Match the rendering style of <Picture 1> exactly — photographic, painted, illustrated or anime.
The SELECTED PANEL COUNT appended below is mandatory. Create exactly that many panels and no more:
- 1 panel: one full-canvas image.
- 2 panels: two equal side-by-side images.
- 3 panels: follow the selected THREE-PANEL LAYOUT PRESET appended below. Use exactly three cells; they are intentionally asymmetrical and do not need equal dimensions.
- 4 panels: a clean 2x2 grid.

Default panel plan:
Panel 1: reproduce the analyzed action pose below as closely as possible, full body visible.
Panel 2: follow the selected PROP USAGE MODE below.
Panel 3: chest-up identity and costume-detail close-up, calm posture.
Panel 4: a clearly different cinematic or environment pose, or another user-requested utility view.

Use only Panels 1 through the selected count and ignore the unused higher-numbered defaults. Every active character panel must use a visibly different body arrangement and camera framing. Use a neutral light-grey studio background unless an enabled environment specifies otherwise. No duplicate or mirrored panel, no merged cell, no pasted source image, no extra person, and no text.

nodes.title: Read First · How To Use This Workflow
widgets_values:
# 🚀 Just follow this order

1. **① LOAD MODELS** — only check that no loader says `MISSING`.
2. **② STAGE 1 INPUT** — drop in one face photo and one outfit photo.
   Cropping is **automatic**; just glance at the two small previews.
3. **③** — only if you want to change body type or styling, or switch to the experimental 4-panel layout. (Optional)
4. Press **Queue** → you get **front / side / back** in one sheet → check it in **⑤**.

**Most of the time you are done here. Stage 2 is OFF by default.**

### If you also want a pose / prop sheet
5. Read **⑥**.
6. Put a pose photo in **⑦**, and type into **⑧** if you want.
7. Flip the switch to **ON** and Queue again.

nodes.title: Stage 2 ON/OFF · How To
widgets_values:
# Stage 2 — use it or not?

**Leave it alone and it stays OFF.** Press Queue and you get just the Stage 1 front / side / back sheet. That is enough for most people.

### If you want Stage 2
1. Put a pose photo into **⑦ STAGE 2 INPUT** below.
2. Turn ON only the prop / background switches you actually need.
3. Type anything extra into **⑧**.
4. Flip `Enable STAGE2_SWITCH` below to **ON**, then Queue.

To go back to Stage 1 only, flip the same switch OFF.

> ⚠️ **Stage 2 needs the resolution in ④ set to `1:1 (Square)`.**
> The final 16:9 composite computes its size assuming a square 3-view input.

nodes.title: Panel Request · Translation Instruction Assembly
widgets_values:
You are a deterministic translator for MiniMax H3 image-generation panel instructions.

Turn the user's panel requests into concise English commands. The requests may be written in any language; if they are already English, keep their meaning and only tighten them.
Normalize every panel label to exactly "Panel N:" where N is 1, 2, 3, or 4.
Labels that mean the same thing include: "Panel 3", "panel3", "3rd panel", "third panel".
Preserve all requested expression, pose, framing, camera, prop, action, and composition details.
For a wink, translate explicitly as one eye fully closed and the other eye open.
Output only the translated "Panel N:" lines. Do not explain, summarize, add headings, or invent requests.
If the user input is empty, output nothing.

- Panels you leave blank use the default. **You do not have to fill them all in.**

📦 Required Models · Downloads
widgets_values:
# 📦 Models you download yourself (5 required + 1 accelerator)

Only grab the ones whose loader on the left says `MISSING`.
Click the link, then put the file in the folder shown, **keeping the original filename**.

## ① H3 Ref2VA base · `models/diffusion_models/`
[minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/diffusion_models/minimax_h3_ref2va_pruned_int8_convrot.safetensors)

## ② Style LoRA · `models/loras/` — OPTIONAL, not required
The loader is **bypassed by default** and the workflow does **not** use a turbo LoRA: speed comes from the 8-step PDD accelerator in ⑦ below.
Only enable a LoRA for **photographic** references, e.g. [h3-realism-people-t2v-i2v-r2v.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/fal/MiniMax-H3-Realism-People-LoRA) (trigger word `r34l1sm`, strength 1.0; 0.6–0.8 for a lighter touch). With illustrated / anime references it pulls the result away from the reference and breaks consistency.

## ③ H3 Qwen text encoder · `models/text_encoders/`
Default (matches the loader): [qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_int8_convrot.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_int8_convrot.safetensors) · ~27 GB
Smaller alternative for 24–32 GB cards: [qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/text_encoders/qwen3vl_32b_minimax_h3_nvfp4_awq.safetensors) · ~16 GB — pick it in the loader after downloading.

## ④ T=1 still-image VAE (for character sheets) · `models/vae/`
[minimax_h3_t1_image_vae_step1597.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Mamad8/MiniMax-H3-Image-VAE/resolve/main/minimax_h3_t1_image_vae_step1597.safetensors)

## ⑤ H3 audio VAE · `models/vae/`
[minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/MiniMax-H3/resolve/main/vae/minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors)

## ⑥ Gemma image analysis · `models/text_encoders/`
[gemma4_e4b_it_fp8_scaled.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/Comfy-Org/Gemma4/resolve/main/text_encoders/gemma4_e4b_it_fp8_scaled.safetensors)

## ⑦ 8-step PDD accelerator · loaded by the `PDD Acc Apply` node
[MiniMax-H3-Ref2VA-Acc-8Step.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/alibaba-pai/MiniMax-H3-Acc-LoRAs) → `models/pdd_acc/`
Node pack: [ComfyUI-MiniMax-H3-PDD-Acc](https://github.com/Jalen-Brunson/ComfyUI-MiniMax-H3-PDD-Acc)

Gemma writes a short description of the pose photo and analyses whichever optional images are switched on. It is **not** used to describe the face or the outfit.

---

## 🤖 These download themselves — do nothing
The models behind the automatic face / outfit cut-out in **② STAGE 1 INPUT**
are **fetched automatically the first time you press Queue.**

- Face cut-out → SAM3

Only grab the ones whose loader on the left says `MISSING`.
Click the link, then put the file in the folder shown, **keeping the original filename**.

## ② Style LoRA · `models/loras/` — OPTIONAL, not required

Only enable a LoRA for **photographic** references, e.g. [h3-realism-people-t2v-i2v-r2v.safetensors](https://huggingface.co/fal/MiniMax-H3-Realism-People-LoRA) (trigger word `r34l1sm`, strength 1.0; 0.6–0.8 for a lighter touch). nodes.title: How To Use · What Each Image Does
widgets_values:
# 📷 You only need 2 photos

- **Left · Face photo** → only the **face and hairstyle** are taken from it. Gender, age and rendering style (photo / anime / illustration) are read from this photo too.
- **Right · Outfit photo** → only **what the person is wearing** is taken from it.

### ✂️ Two automatic steps: remove background → extract clothes
The outfit photo first has its **background removed entirely**, then only the **clothes, shoes and socks** are cut out.
Face, hair, arms and legs drop out on their own, so **you do not need to crop below the neck first.**

> ⚠️ **Keep everything except the outfit out of the outfit photo.**
> Laundry on the floor, bags, or shoes lying around get read as "clothing" and end up mixed into the result.
> Background removal catches most of it, but anything touching the person can survive.

> ⚠️ **Both shoes and both arms must be visible in the outfit photo.**
> Only what survives the cut-out is transferred. If one foot is hidden, the sheet will also show only one shoe.
> Hats, sunglasses and bags are dropped by default — tick `Hat` / `Sunglasses` / `Bag` on the **Extract Clothes Only** node if you want them.

> ⚠️ **Bigger photos are better — aim for 1000px wide or more.**
> In small photos, fine parts like socks and shoes break up.

### 🛟 If the cut-out fails
Two switches sit under the previews. **Face Source ON** sends the raw face photo instead of the SAM3 crop; **Outfit Source ON** sends the background-removed full photo instead of the clothes cut-out. The previews always show what H3 actually receives.
Long hair, buns or a hat cut off? Change the SAM3 prompt from `head` to `head and hair` (or `head and hat`).

### 👀 How to check it worked
Look at the two small previews on the right. If you see **only a head** / **only clothes** floating on grey, it worked.
If part of the outfit is missing, adjust the checkboxes on the **Extract Clothes Only** node.
Note that **socks are picked up by `Left-shoe` / `Right-shoe`** — leave those two ON even for a socks-only photo.

### 👟 To change shoes / socks / bare feet
The prompt forces **nothing** about feet. It simply follows the photo.
To change it, type into **③** — that input has the highest priority.
e.g. `white ankle socks, no shoes` / `black loafers` / `barefoot`

Body type and styling go in the same box.
e.g. `slim adult female build, narrow shoulders, slender arms and legs`

nodes.title: Stage 1 Prompt · Base (3-view / 4-panel) + User Direction
widgets_values:
subject_definitions:
<Subject 1> is the adult person seen in <Picture 1>. Their reference role is IDENTITY ONLY: face, facial geometry, eyes, nose, lips, skin tone, apparent age, apparent gender presentation and hairstyle, including hair length, colour, texture and parting. Read the gender presentation, apparent age, skin tone and visible facial features directly from <Picture 1> and keep them unchanged.

<Subject 2> is the outfit shown in <Picture 2>. Its reference role is WARDROBE ONLY: garment shapes, cut, length, colours, patterns, materials, whatever is worn on the feet, and wearable accessories.

summary:
[reference generation] Create one static character turnaround sheet showing <Subject 1> wearing the wardrobe from <Subject 2>. Present exactly three complete full-body views — front, strict right-side profile and back — on a neutral light-grey studio background, rendered in the same visual style as <Picture 1>.

retention_analysis:
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2], [Shot 3]): fully_preserved - the same person from <Picture 1> appears in every shot. Preserve the exact face, facial geometry, eyes, nose, lips, skin tone, apparent age, gender presentation and hairstyle.

The hairstyle comes exclusively from <Picture 1> and remains identical in all three shots: same length, cut, parting, colour and texture. Only its viewing direction changes. Do not transfer clothing, pose, framing, lighting or background from <Picture 1>.

<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1], [Shot 2], [Shot 3]): attribute_transfer - transfer only the garments, colours, patterns, materials, whatever is worn on the feet, and wearable accessories from <Picture 2> onto <Subject 1>.

Do not transfer the outfit donor’s face, hair, hairstyle, age, gender presentation, shoulder width, muscle mass, torso volume, height, limb thickness, body shape, pose or background. <Picture 2> is a wardrobe reference only. <Subject 1> wears the outfit but never inherits the outfit donor’s identity or body.

detailed_description:
The target is one still image, not a video. Match the rendering style of <Picture 1> exactly — photographic, painted, illustrated or anime — including its line quality, shading, colour treatment and level of detail; never convert an illustrated or anime reference into a photograph, and never convert a photograph into an illustration. Use a neutral light-grey seamless background with even soft lighting.

Arrange exactly three equal vertical views side by side from left to right. All three views must share one ground line, one subject scale, one camera distance, one camera height and one lighting setup.

[Shot 1] Complete full-body front view in a relaxed A-pose, face looking directly toward the camera. Both feet point forward and are fully visible.

[Shot 2] Complete full-body strict 90-degree right-side profile view. The head, torso, hips and feet all face directly toward the side of the frame. Both feet are fully visible in true side profile.

[Shot 3] Complete full-body back view photographed from directly behind. The subject and both feet point away from the viewer, and both feet are fully visible from the rear. Never turn the feet back toward the camera and never reuse the front view.

The same hairstyle from <Picture 1> must remain visible in all three shots and change only according to the viewing direction. Show the complete head and both complete feet in every shot.

Keep the face uncovered. Do not add a helmet or mask. Do not create an extra panel, action pose, separate product display, inset, duplicate cell, caption, label, logo or text.

CANONICAL BODY LOCK — applies unless the user explicitly requests a different body build:
All three views are rotations of one unchanged adult body mesh.

Keep identical height, head-to-body ratio, shoulder width, chest volume, waist width, hip width, arm length, leg length, limb thickness, hand size and foot size in all three views.

Use the same relaxed A-pose, stance and weight distribution in every view. Only the viewing direction changes.

Use a fixed orthographic-like 85–105 mm lens, identical camera height, camera distance, ground line and subject scale. Never redraw a wider, shorter, taller, heavier, slimmer or differently proportioned body between views.

USER STAGE 1 DIRECTION — HIGHEST PRIORITY:
The user instruction that follows outranks every default written above. Follow it literally and in full. It may override body build, skin tone, complexion, presentation, framing, styling, and anything worn, including what is or is not on the feet. Where it conflicts with any line above, the user instruction wins.

The only things it never changes are the <Subject 1> identity role (face and hair come from <Picture 1>) and the three-shot front / side / back layout.

When a skin tone is specified, apply it consistently to every visible area of skin in all three shots.

If nothing follows this line, there is no user direction: keep every rule above exactly as written.
